- vercel.json `api/**/*.ts` turns every test and prompt file under api/ into a function; use `api/*.ts` and a .vercelignore, with a test guarding the count.

- A sync spec must name the timestamp owner (client updated_at for LWW, server synced_at for the pull cursor) and map every local field to a column before an executor sees it; T-0067 found eleven gaps in a spec that left them implicit.

Design rule: the app stays fully usable signed out and offline; the account only adds sync. Only VITE_SUPABASE_URL and VITE_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY are client-side.

Auth contract (T-0064, do not modify src/auth/auth.tsx or src/sync/supabase.ts): useAuth() {status: disabled|loading|signed_out|signed_in, userId, address, signIn, signUp, signOut}; all network goes through `withSession(fn(client, userId))` which returns null when signed out, unconfigured or unreadable and refreshes a session expiring within 30 s.

Model: local is the source of truth for the UI. Every local write bumps updated_at and enqueues an outbox entry; the engine pushes the outbox then pulls rows changed on the server since the per-table cursor; conflicts are last-write-wins (LWW) on the client updated_at, enforced on the server by a trigger (F1) and on the client at merge; deletes are tombstones (deleted_at). Amendments E1..E11 answer spec review T-0067, F1..F16 answer spec review T-0069; F wins over E, E wins over anything else.

E1 Timestamps. The client owns updated_at (ISO with ms, set on every local write from Date.now()). New migration supabase/migrations/20261010170000_sync_columns.sql: add `synced_at timestamptz not null default now()` to profiles, items, scenes, conversations; `drop trigger if exists set_updated_at on public.<t>` for the four tables and `drop function if exists public.set_updated_at()`; new function public.sync_guard() (F1) with `create trigger sync_guard before insert or update on public.<t> for each row execute function public.sync_guard()` on the four tables; indexes <t>_user_id_synced_at_idx on (user_id, synced_at); add to items: `place text, object_id text, image_path text`; add to conversations: `place text`. F14: the init migration is not edited, not even its comment; the Clerk-to-Supabase-Auth note goes into docs/SUPABASE.md. Upserts never send synced_at or user_id (server defaults fill them; user_id from auth.jwt() sub, the same value withSession passes as userId). schema.ts: SyncColumns gains synced_at; ItemRow gains place, object_id, image_path; ConversationRow gains place.
F1 Server LWW guard. public.sync_guard(): on update, `if new.updated_at < old.updated_at then return null; end if;` (the stale write is skipped silently, PostgREST returns no error); then `new.synced_at = now(); return new;` for insert and update. The client never relies on push order: the pull after a skipped push brings the newer server row and client LWW keeps it. docs/SYNC.md explains the guard. engine.test.ts: an older local write whose upsert resolves is removed from the outbox, and the following pull with the newer remote row replaces the local one.
F2 Rollback SQL. supabase/rollback/20261010170000_sync_columns.down.sql (outside supabase/migrations so the CLI never applies it): drop the sync_guard triggers and function, recreate public.set_updated_at() and the four set_updated_at triggers exactly as in the init migration, drop the four synced_at indexes, drop the columns synced_at (four tables), items.place/object_id/image_path, conversations.place. docs/SUPABASE.md says to apply it in the SQL editor after `git revert` of the merge. Not relying on git revert for the database.
F3 migrations.test.ts rewritten to check the net schema by text: keep every existing init assertion unchanged; read the sync_columns file and assert per table: a `drop trigger if exists set_updated_at on public.<t>`, a `create trigger sync_guard before insert or update on public.<t>`, an `add column synced_at timestamptz not null default now()`; assert `drop function if exists public.set_updated_at` and `create or replace function public.sync_guard()` containing `new.updated_at < old.updated_at`; assert the count of `create trigger set_updated_at` in the init file equals the count of `drop trigger if exists set_updated_at` in the new file (net: no updated_at trigger survives); assert the items and conversations columns; assert the rollback file exists and contains `create trigger set_updated_at` four times and `drop trigger if exists sync_guard` four times.

E2 Pull cursor. alltag.sync.meta = {ownerId, cursors: {items, conversations}, lastSyncedAt}. Pull per table: `select('*').gte('synced_at', cursor).order('synced_at').order('id').range(i, i+499)` until a page is shorter than 500; merge every row by LWW on updated_at; F4: compare as milliseconds via Date.parse on both sides (map.ts normalises every remote updated_at and deleted_at to `new Date(x).toISOString()`), equal ms: remote wins, idempotent. F10: the cursor becomes (max synced_at seen minus 60 s) as ISO, written only after all pages of that table merged; merges are idempotent so the overlap is safe. A failed pull leaves the cursor unchanged. A missing cursor pulls everything. Tests: '+00:00' vs 'Z' inputs and a microsecond timestamp ('2026-10-10T14:00:00.123456+00:00') compare correctly; the written cursor equals max minus 60 s.

E3 Entities and mappings. No scene record in U3; the scenes table stays unused (say so in docs/SYNC.md). Synced tables: items and conversations only; profiles/settings sync is out of U3. Card <-> ItemRow: id<->id; phrase_fr; phrase_en ''<->null; noun_fr/objectId/errorType/place <-> noun_fr/object_id/error_type/place with undefined<->null; ease/interval/reps/due(ms) <-> srs {ease, interval, reps, due ISO}; learnedAt(ms) <-> kept_at ISO; crop stays local only; image_path (E4) <-> image_path; updated_at, deleted_at. Conversation <-> ConversationRow: id; startedAt<->started_at; durationS<->duration_s; lines; keptCount<->kept_count; place; updated_at, deleted_at. Add optional `updated_at?: string; deleted_at?: string | null; image_path?: string | null` to Card and `updated_at?: string; deleted_at?: string | null` to Conversation in src/lib/types.ts. Mapping functions live in src/sync/map.ts with round-trip tests. Ids are UUIDs everywhere: newId() in store.ts and conversations.ts falls back to a Math.random-based RFC 4122 v4 string when crypto.randomUUID is missing; no `card-`/`conv-` ids remain. F16 (verified by the Planner with git grep on goal/T-0001): the only producers of `card-`/`conv-` ids are store.ts:50 and conversations.ts:45; no reader depends on the prefix; store.clear() is called only from Settings.tsx:49; nothing outside tests calls store.remove or conversations.remove. docs/SYNC.md documents clock skew (a device with a fast clock wins conflicts; U3 accepts this).

E4 Images. Upload from Card.crop. F11 (definite): nothing in the app bounds the frame today (git grep finds no toDataURL or canvas under src; Scene.tsx:67 sets crop from session.frame, the raw file-input data URL). So src/sync/images.ts exports `shrinkDataUrl(dataUrl, 1280)`: via an Image and a canvas, JPEG quality 0.85, long side at most 1280 px; when `document.createElement('canvas').getContext('2d')` returns null (jsdom) or decoding fails, return the input unchanged. The engine calls it at upload time only; Look.tsx, session.ts and api.ts stay unchanged (capture keeps the full frame for Gemini). Path `<userId>/<sha256 hex of the shrunk data URL>.jpg` (crypto.subtle.digest), so cards kept from the same frame share one object; the engine keeps `alltag.sync.uploaded` (array of paths) and skips an upload already listed; the list is never pruned and orphaned objects stay after a tombstone (documented; resetLocal clears the list). Order per card: upload (storage.from('scenes').upload(path, blob, {upsert: true, contentType: 'image/jpeg'})) then upsert the row with image_path; an upload failure fails that entry (E6) and the row is not pushed. Data URL to Blob via fetch(dataUrl).blob() with a fallback that decodes base64 by hand (tests use the fallback). Pulled cards store image_path only. F12: `useCardImage(card)` in src/sync/images.ts returns card.crop when present; otherwise, with a SyncProvider mounted, a signed URL through the provider's withSession (createSignedUrl(path, 3600), cached per path for the session), or null offline; with no provider it returns card.crop ?? null and makes no calls. Diary.tsx and Review.tsx render the image through a small `CardImage` component (one hook per component, never inside a map) with the existing placeholder when null; the existing Diary and Review tests stay green without providers. Quota: F15: src/sync/local.ts owns the flag: `export function storageFull(): boolean`; collection writes set it on a thrown setItem and clear it on the next successful write; status() reports it as state 'error', reason 'storage_full'; local.test.ts asserts set then clear.

E5 Soft delete. store.remove and conversations.remove tombstone the row (deleted_at = updated_at = now ISO) and enqueue; all/get/due/byNoun and conversations.all hide tombstones; replaceFromRemote keeps tombstones. clear() stays a hard local reset (tests and the Settings reset) and also drops that table's outbox and dead entries; it enqueues nothing. F7: local purge on load drops tombstones older than 30 days only when the row has no outbox or dead entry. Server tombstones are not purged in U3 (documented). There is one outbox op: the row state at drain time is what gets upserted, tombstone included; no DELETE requests.

E6 Outbox and push policy. src/sync/outbox.ts: alltag.outbox = [{table, id, at, attempts, lastError?}]; enqueue keeps one entry per (table,id) and sets at = now; drain(fn) processes in enqueue order and removes an entry only when fn resolved AND the stored `at` still equals the drained `at` (a write during the drain survives and is pushed next run). F5/F6 failure classes, read from the response, never from the PostgREST error object: fn returns the supabase response `{data, error, status}`; a thrown exception, or a response with error and no numeric status, is a network failure: the entry is kept, attempts unchanged, run state 'offline' when navigator.onLine is false else 'error'. A response with error and status 401, 408, 429 or >= 500: attempts+1, kept. attempts >= 5 or any other 4xx: moved to alltag.outbox.dead with lastError. A missing local row drops the entry. Storage upload errors: a numeric `status` or `statusCode` on the error classifies as above, otherwise network. Dead entries resurrect: `engine.retryDead()` moves every dead entry back to the outbox with attempts 0 and syncs; it runs on every transition to signed_in and from the Settings button "retry n changes" (shown when dead > 0). Test mocks return the `{data, error, status}` shape. F9 single flight: sync() returns the in-flight promise while running; any trigger during a run sets a dirty flag and exactly one more run starts when the current one finishes (engine.test.ts: a write during the push results in a second run, a third trigger does not add a fourth). If any entry stayed in the outbox after the push, state = 'error' (or 'offline') with the last error message and the pull is skipped this run; dead entries do not block the pull. status() = {state: 'off'|'idle'|'syncing'|'error'|'offline', reason?: 'disabled'|'signed_out'|'other_account'|'storage_full'|'kill_switch', lastSyncedAt, pending: outbox length, dead: dead length, error?: string}. Multi-tab writes are not coordinated (documented).

E7 Owner binding. On the transition to signed_in with userId: ownerId unset -> adopt (ownerId = userId) and enqueue every non-tombstone local items and conversations row once (initial full push), then sync. ownerId === userId -> retryDead then sync. ownerId !== userId -> state 'off', reason 'other_account', nothing pushed or pulled; Settings shows "this device keeps data from another account" and a button "clear local data and sync this account". F13: the button is two-step: the first click shows "n unsynced changes will be lost. clear anyway?" (n = pending + dead; "nothing unsynced" when 0) with "clear" and "keep"; only "clear" calls engine.resetLocal() (clears alltag.cards, alltag.conversations, alltag.outbox, alltag.outbox.dead, alltag.sync.uploaded, alltag.sync.meta) then adopts and syncs. signOut keeps local data, the outbox and ownerId, and clears only cursors and lastSyncedAt.

E8 Migration of existing local data, non-destructive and idempotent: on first load of alltag.cards or alltag.conversations in the new shape, copy the raw string once to alltag.cards.v0 / alltag.conversations.v0 if that key is absent, then fill missing updated_at (learnedAt or startedAt, else now), deleted_at null, and replace non-UUID ids with new UUIDs, and persist. F8: if the .v0 write throws, the migration is not persisted this load: the raw rows are used in memory with updated_at defaulted at read time and ids untouched, storageFull is set (status 'error', 'storage_full'), and the engine makes no network calls while storageFull is set, so no non-UUID id reaches the server; the next load retries. The kill switch does not skip this migration (local-only, idempotent, .v0 is the rollback); documented. Kill switch: localStorage alltag.sync.disabled = '1' or import.meta.env.VITE_SYNC_DISABLED = '1' -> state 'off', reason 'kill_switch', no triggers, no network; Settings hides "sync now" then. Rollback: `git revert` the merge plus the F2 rollback SQL; local data: the .v0 keys.
